notes:
### Research Notes

#### 1. What the product does
Sherlock is an open-source command-line intelligence (OSINT) tool written in Python that allows users to search for social media accounts across hundreds of websites simultaneously using a single username. It automates username enumeration by constructing profile URLs and checking server responses to determine if an account exists.
* **Source URL:** https://github.com/sherlock-project/sherlock
* **Verbatim Quote:** `hunt down social media accounts by username across social networks`
* **Source URL:** https://sherlockproject.xyz/
* **Verbatim Quote:** `sherlock hunt down social media accounts by username across 400+ social networks`

#### 2. Every auth method of the public API and which one a multi-tenant integration would use
The core Sherlock project does not provide an official hosted public API. It is a command-line tool that performs direct web requests without requiring any authentication. An experimental, unmaintained REST API repository exists for local deployment, but it is not a public cloud service. However, community-maintained versions are hosted as "Actors" on the Apify platform, which expose a public REST API authenticated via Apify API tokens.
* **primary_auth:** `none` (for the native open-source CLI tool) or `api_key` (if utilizing third-party community hosting via Apify).
* **Source URL:** https://bellingcat.gitbook.io/toolkit/more/all-tools/sherlock
* **Verbatim Quote:** `Outdated API: There is no official Sherlock API. An experimental REST API exists but has not been maintained since 2021, and using it requires local setup.`
* **Source URL:** https://bellingcat.gitbook.io/toolkit/more/all-tools/sherlock
* **Verbatim Quote:** `No account/API keys needed – Sherlock uses direct web requests and does not require creating any account or API key to use.`
* **Source URL:** https://apify.com/misceres/sherlock/api
* **Verbatim Quote:** `To use the Apify API, you'll need an Apify account and your API token, found in API & Integrations in Apify Console.`

#### 3. Exactly how a developer gets credentials and what it costs
Because Sherlock is an open-source project, developers do not need to obtain credentials or pay any fees to use the core software; they can simply clone the repository or install it via package managers to run it locally or self-host it. If a developer prefers to use the community-hosted API on Apify, they can sign up for an Apify account to get an API token. Apify provides a free tier with usage credits, alongside paid subscription plans.
* **access:** `self_serve_free`
* **Source URL:** https://bellingcat.gitbook.io/toolkit/more/all-tools/sherlock
* **Verbatim Quote:** `the latest version is published on PyPI for one-command install (e.g. pipx install sherlock-project or pip install --user sherlock-project ). There is also an official Docker image available`
* **Source URL:** https://apify.com/misceres/sherlock/api
* **Verbatim Quote:** `sherlock pricing pricing pay per usage try for free go to apify store`

#### 4. API style, breadth, OpenAPI spec, webhooks, sandbox
* **API Style:** There is no official hosted public API. The unmaintained experimental repository (`sherlock-project/api`) uses Django REST Framework (REST) but requires local hosting. Third-party Apify actors provide a REST API interface.
* **Breadth:** Extremely narrow; the tool performs a single function—enumerating a username across 400+ websites.
* **OpenAPI Spec:** No official OpenAPI specification is provided by the core project. (Apify automatically generates OpenAPI definitions for its hosted community actors).
* **Webhooks:** Not natively supported by the CLI tool.
* **Sandbox:** Not applicable, as the tool is open-source and can be run entirely within a local or containerized sandbox environment.
* **Source URL:** https://bellingcat.gitbook.io/toolkit/more/all-tools/sherlock
* **Verbatim Quote:** `Sherlock is primarily a CLI tool, so some familiarity with the command line is required to install and run it.`
* **Source URL:** https://docs.apify.com/api/v2
* **Verbatim Quote:** `get openapi definition`

#### 5. MCP servers
* **mcp:** `community_only`
* **Details:** There is no official Model Context Protocol (MCP) server published by the Sherlock Project organization. However, there is a community-created MCP server (`Burnsedia/sherlock-mcp`) that wraps the tool using FastMCP. *(Note: Another repository, `H4RR1SON/sherlock-mcp`, is an official MCP server for a separate threat intelligence platform called Covertlabs and is unrelated to this open-source project).*
* **Source URL:** https://github.com/Burnsedia/sherlock-mcp
* **Verbatim Quote:** `sherlock mcp server: fastmcp integration for social media username searches across 400+ platforms using model context protocol.`

#### 6. Buildability verdict with the main blocker
* **verdict:** `ready_with_friction`
* **Main Blocker:** `local_cli_only`
* **Explanation:** Sherlock is an open-source command-line tool and library rather than a hosted SaaS application with an official public API. To build an AI agent toolkit today, Composio would need to wrap the Python CLI/library and execute it locally inside a secure sandbox environment, or rely on third-party community-hosted endpoints on Apify.
* **Source URL:** https://bellingcat.gitbook.io/toolkit/more/all-tools/sherlock
* **Verbatim Quote:** `Sherlock is primarily a CLI tool, so some familiarity with the command line is required to install and run it.`
